answer: The lagoon admits only lit vessels: every boat on anchor watch hangs a lantern, and a dark hull is a smuggler - presence in the shelter must be visible to every watch. Each watch owes a night story, newly invented: the harbor clerk hashes every tale, so a fable retold from an older night fails the ledger - imagination is the toll for anchoring. Lanterns prove you are there; stories prove someone awake is steering; together they keep out ghost ships. Farms anchor dark and repeat one tale nightly; the hash ledger eats them. Honest vessels hang light, invent fresh, let the ledger keep the water.
